problems.description: A face's entire boundary has collapsed within tolerance to a single point: every wire vertex is coincident (or the outer wire's bounding box is smaller than the working precision), so the face has no usable 2D interior and contributes nothing to the shape's area/volume. OCCT detects this ('spot face') and repairs it by merging all of the face's vertices into one shared tolerant vertex and deleting the face and its edges from the shell.

problems.description: A face has degenerated into a zero-width sliver/ribbon: either (a) it is bounded by exactly two long edges plus tiny connecting edges, and the two long edges run coincident within tolerance along their full length, or (b) the underlying BSpline/Bezier surface's control-point grid collapses to within tolerance across an entire row/column in one parametric direction. OCCT detects this ('strip face') and repairs it by merging the two coincident long edges into one shared edge, deleting the strip face and its short connecting edges, and removing any shell that becomes empty as a result.

problems.description: A face contains a vertex that is NOT an endpoint of a given edge of that same face, but whose 3D position projects within tolerance onto the interior of that edge's curve (a geometric T-junction/self-touch that isn't expressed as shared topology). OCCT detects this ('splitting vertex') and repairs it by inserting a synthetic splitting edge from the vertex to its projected point and dividing the face into two independently valid sub-faces along it.
occt_evidence: ShapeAnalysis_CheckSmallFace::CheckSplittingVertices — ShapeAnalysis_CheckSmallFace.cxx:487 @ bd2a789f15235755ce4d1a3b07379a2e062fdc2e (line verified; V3 cited 687, drift ~200 lines). Key logic: line 533 `if (V.IsSame(V1) || V.IsSame(V2)) continue;` -- a vertex that is already a topological endpoint of the edge being tested is explicitly skipped.
subvariants: vertex sits on the interior of an edge belonging to a different wire of the same face (outer/inner T-junction)
vertex sits on the interior of an edge of the same wire
problems.notes: Catalog contains ~17 fixtures explicitly titled after ShapeAnalysis_CheckSmallFace.CheckSplittingVertices / ShapeFix_Face.FixSplitFace (Tfa010, Tfa079, Tfa094, Tfa104, Tfa117, Tfa129, Tfa149, Tfa169, etc.) but reading 4 of them directly (Tfa010, Tfa079, Tfa104, Tfa129) shows a consistent mismatch: in every sampled fixture the 'splitting' vertex is encoded as a genuine shared topological ENDPOINT of the edges it touches (the bottom edge is literally split into two EDGE_CURVEs at that vertex, or the vertex is reused as an edge_curve endpoint across both wires), which is exactly the case CheckSplittingVertices explicitly SKIPS (`V.IsSame(V1) || V.IsSame(V2)`); Tfa129 additionally has no extra vertex encoded in the STEP at all despite its comment describing one. None of the sampled fixtures place an independent vertex near (but not attached to) an unrelated edge's curve interior, which is the actual trigger condition. Also note ShapeFix_FixSmallFace::FixSplitFace/SplitOneFace are not called by the class's own default Perform() (which only calls FixSpotFace+FixStripFace) -- they must be invoked explicitly, though this doesn't affect the verdict since the method still exists as real OCCT healing code. Recommend re-authoring this family with a vertex geometrically near an unrelated edge's interior without being declared as its topological endpoint.

problems.description: A compound/comp-solid contains one or more degenerate 'sliver' solids -- artifacts of Boolean/import operations whose volume is below an application-supplied threshold, and/or whose width factor (volume divided by half its surface area, a proxy for 'thinness') is below a threshold. OCCT repairs this by either deleting the sliver solid outright, or merging it into an adjacent non-small solid (folding its non-shared faces into the neighbor's shell).

problems.description: A vertex, edge, or face carries a tolerance value that falls outside an application-specified acceptable range [tmin, tmax] -- either unrealistically tight (masking nothing, but inconsistent with the rest of the model) or excessively loose (hiding real geometric gaps/deviations downstream). OCCT repairs this by clamping the offending tolerance to the nearer bound of the range, recursing through WIRE->EDGE/VERTEX or whole-shape hierarchies as needed.

problems.description: Two (or more) faces that geometrically share a boundary curve each carry their own separate copy of that boundary's edges/vertices, so the shell's free (single-face) boundary edges are geometrically coincident but topologically disjoint -- either exactly coincident (pure duplicate) or separated by a small gap that is larger than the sewing tolerance but within an application-specified closing tolerance. OCCT repairs this by classifying the shell's free boundary into closed/open wire groups, then (when a closing tolerance is supplied that exceeds the sewing tolerance) connecting nearby open-wire endpoints and replacing/merging the corresponding vertices in the underlying edges so the boundary becomes topologically continuous.

problems.description: A shell's constituent faces have inconsistent orientation relative to each other -- some faces are flipped relative to a globally-consistent (outward-facing) convention, possibly combined with exact-duplicate faces, edges shared by three or more faces (non-manifold connectivity), or a mismatch between the shell's cached Closed flag and its actual free-edge state. OCCT repairs this by regrouping/reorienting the shell's faces into one or more consistently-oriented shells (splitting into multiple shells when a single consistent orientation can't be achieved across all faces), dropping exact-duplicate faces during the rebuild, optionally special-casing non-manifold multi-shared edges so they don't force incompatible faces into the same group, and correcting the Closed flag when it disagrees with the detected free-boundary state.

problems.description: A solid built from a single closed shell has its overall orientation globally inverted: every face is consistently flipped together, so classifying a point at infinity against the resulting solid reports it as 'inside' (i.e. the shell bounds the complement of the intended region -- material and void are swapped). OCCT repairs this by reversing the entire shell (all faces at once) so the solid's interior/exterior classification comes out correct.

problems.description: A shape intended to become a solid is built from more than one shell without pre-established outer-boundary/void nesting -- e.g. an unstructured compound of shells that should really be recognized as either (a) an outer boundary shell plus nested internal cavity shell(s) forming one valid solid, or (b) multiple disjoint solids incorrectly bundled together. OCCT repairs this by point-containment classification (BRepClass3d_SolidClassifier) of each shell against the others to determine nesting/disjointness, then reconstructing one or more properly-formed TopoDS_Solid(s) (or a compound of separate solids when the shells don't share one containment structure).

line_verification_notes: Significant line drift throughout: ShapeAnalysis_CheckSmallFace.cxx entries in V3 were cited against a version of the file with ~90-250 extra lines relative to the pinned V7_8_1 source (e.g. CheckPin cited at 852-901 vs actual 601; CheckPinFace at 1069 vs actual 742; CheckPinEdges at 1208-1308 vs actual 836; CheckStripFace at 659 vs actual 456). ShapeFix_Shell.cxx drift was extreme: V3 cited FixFaceOrientation at line 1428, but the entire file is only 1114 lines long in the pinned commit -- the real function starts at line 844. ShapeFix_Solid.cxx also drifted (~86-130 lines): Perform cited at 461 vs actual 375, SolidFromShell at 656 vs actual 538. ShapeFix_FixSmallFace.cxx and ShapeFix_FixSmallSolid.cxx, ShapeFix_ShapeTolerance.cxx, ShapeFix_FreeBounds.cxx, ShapeFix_Shape.cxx line citations were close to accurate (drift under ~10 lines) since those files' method-line V3 entries already used the correct definitions with 'Line: File.cxx:NNNN' format; I re-verified all of them directly and cite the confirmed lines above. Two V3 claims were found factually WRONG against current source and corrected: (1) ShapeFix_Shell.FixFaceOrientation.duplicate_faces_undetected claimed duplicates are 'still processed independently' -- source shows they ARE deduplicated (aMapAdded.Add failing silently drops them from Lface); (2) ShapeFix_Solid.Perform.single_shell_orientation_skip claimed the multi-shell case (NbShells != 1) skips orientation fixing entirely -- source shows it instead dispatches to a more general CreateSolids/CollectSolids point-containment classification (this became the basis for the separately-tracked GAP problem tkshh-solid-unstructured-multishell). Beyond citation verification, reading ShapeFix_FixSmallFace.cxx directly surfaced that FixPinFace (line 753-756) is a literal no-op stub and that CheckPin/CheckPinFace/CheckPinEdges/CheckTwisted in ShapeAnalysis_CheckSmallFace.cxx are never called anywhere else in the OCCT source tree (confirmed via grep across /tmp/cad-occt-781/src) -- V3 did not call this out explicitly as dead code, so the whole Pin/Twisted detection family was excluded rather than promoted to a GAP problem, since there is no OCCT healing code that could ever fix it. Fixture-side verification also caught a mismatch V3 could not have found (it only analyzes OCCT source, not the fixture corpus): the ~17 catalog fixtures titled after ShapeAnalysis_CheckSmallFace.CheckSplittingVertices consistently encode the wrong geometric pattern (a genuinely shared topological vertex/endpoint rather than an independent vertex merely near an unrelated edge's interior), so tkshh-splitting-vertex-face is marked GAP despite substantial fixture-count coverage by title alone.
